newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya turns coffee auction into exchange in reform.
newsitem.headline: Kenya turns coffee auction into exchange in reform.

text.p: Kenya's weekly coffee export auction has been turned into a coffee exchange under which planters will be able to fix reserve prices in the latest reform of Kenya's coffee marketing, the Coffee Board of Kenya said.

The board said in a statement that an exchange was necessary in order to allow fixing of reserve prices by planters through their licensed brokers. In addition balloting will take place each week on which auctioneers operate the auction.
The statement said nothing about ownership of the exchange.
Currently export auctions are conducted by Kenya Cofffee Auctions Ltd, in which the board has a 70 percent shareholding.
Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae has previously said he wanted the coffee board's shareholding cut to a minority stake.

Guidelines posted by the board for planters who wanted to fix reserve prices for their coffee included appointment of brokers and their registration with the board of the Mild Coffee Trade Association of Eastern Africa.
"Balloting of floor auctioneers at the Nairobi Coffee Exchange shall be implemented with immediate effect," the board said, adding that a central auction structure still remained.
"This aspect of our operations at the Nairobi Coffee Exchange will enhance its transparency and accountability to the coffee growers and the public at large," the board added.

On the appointment and operations of licensed brokers, the board said in its guidelines that planters would have discretion on the appointments and would provide the board with a certified copy of their contract agreement.

"As a measure of liberalisation, planters will be at liberty to negotiate brokerage charges with their respective brokers. Such charges should be clearly stipulated within the brokerage contract," the board said.

It added that such planters would have a right to fix reserve prices at the Nairobi Coffee Exchange (NCE). It said, "... in this respect, all coffee that enters a sales catalogue with a "Planters Registered Distinguishing Mark' would be eligible for fixing of reserve prices by the planter's-appointed brokers".
"However, due to technical and operational requirements, the board would continue fixing reserve prices for coffee that falls within the category of parchment bulks and clean coffee bulks."
The board said a planter which did not appoint an independent broker for fixing reserve prices for eligible coffee would be represented by the board, as previously.
The board said it would programme all coffee for sale by a first-in-first-out (FIFO) basis, irrespective of whether its reserve price was fixed by the planters' brokers or the board.

"The appointed (planters' brokers) will have the option to fix reserve prices for eligible lots of coffee within a sales catalogue and communicate the same to the board for transmission to the board's contracted Broker/Auctioneers at the Nairobi Coffee Exchange (NCE) before the commencement of the auction."

Any coffee lot whose reserve price has been fixed by planters' brokers could be withdrawn from being sold only twice if the fixed reserve price had not been attained at the two respective auctions, the coffee board said.

But such withdrawal would be subject to the discretion of the planters'-appointed brokers authorizing the sale of coffee lot(s) through an auctions sub-committee, and using the highest price noted by the floor auctioneers as a guide.
